meta.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 · AI/ML · community · run 1
meta.note: Main run, 60 minutes. The verifier accepted 3 of 6 credited claims; 2 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

agents.brief: Goal: a prediction claim on CIFAR-10 beating the 6% error reference (lab data /lab/data/cifar10, baseline script /lab/data/baselines/train_cifar.py). Use a fast airbench/ResNet-9-style CNN (BatchNorm, label smoothing, SGD/Nesterov or OneCycle, flip+crop augmentation, ~30-60 epochs) run via lab exec on the GPU. Hold out 5k of train for a metrics.json val error (no EVAL_DIR). With EVAL_DIR, train on all 50k, save weights to OUT_DIR (keep small, fp16) and write predictions.csv (id,pred). Publish a finding with a prediction test (test.inputs = your weights blob). Time budget is about 45 minutes; publish by minute 45 even if the margin is small. Do not claim numbers that no exec produced.

artifacts.title: ResNet-9 style CNN, 30 epochs, reaches 5.36% held-out error on CIFAR-10
artifacts.summary: Residual ResNet-9 style net (conv-BN-ReLU, two residual blocks), label smoothing 0.2, one-cycle SGD-Nesterov, reflect-pad crop + flip augmentation, fp16 autocast, flip TTA. Holdout: train on 45k, evaluate on 5k held-out train images (exec-53f6b41c, val_error 0.0536). Final model: retrained on all 50k (exec-a5951729), weights saved as fp16 and used for the prediction test on the official 10k test set.

artifacts.title: LinearSVC on word+char TF-IDF beats the strongest TF-IDF+LR we tested on AG News
artifacts.summary: 5-fold stratified CV on the 40k training set: LinearSVC (word 1-3 + char_wb 2-5, C=0.3) 8.13%; word 1-2 LR (C=10) 9.03%; word 1-2 LR (C=3) 9.10%; word 1-2 LR (C=30) 9.16%; word 1-2 + char LR (C=10) 8.70%. The test retrains the strongest LR on all 40k and compares both arms on the official test set.

events.text: I need to learn the lab's conventions before deciding what to investigate. I'll start with the guide, the data READMEs and the baselines.

The guide is clear. Before choosing a direction I need the baseline README, the CIFAR baseline script, the artifact schema, and whether any pretrained models or GPU libraries exist offline. Those determine what is feasible in about 55 minutes.

About 55 minutes remain. AG News is the cheapest route to a `prediction` claim: a TF-IDF word plus char n-gram linear model should beat the 8% TF-IDF+LR comparator, and it runs on CPU in minutes. I'll recruit one researcher to attempt CIFAR-10 below 6% error with a fast GPU model, then write and run the AG News experiment myself.
I need the lab guide, the CIFAR-10 README and the baseline script before designing anything. Starting there.

The AG News baseline is cheap to beat on CPU, so I'll build that claim myself. First I need the full worked example, which was truncated earlier, to match the test invocation format.

tr = pd.r

I'll write a ResNet-9 style trainer with GPU-side flip and crop augmentation, label smoothing and a one-cycle schedule. It will hold out 5k for a val error without EVAL_DIR, and with EVAL_DIR it trains on all 50k, saves fp16 weights, and writes predictions. I'll also write a predict-only script for the test. Then I'll check the schema and start the holdout run in the background.

The last command hit a stray `</parameter>` tag, so bash died at the final `sleep` line. The earlier lines ran, so the `nohup` holdout job may already be going. I'll check the log, the GPU and the run list before changing anything.
Launching the 30-epoch holdout run in the background so it doesn't block the shell. I'll check the log after a short wait.

The best candidate is LinearSVC (C=0.3) on word 1-3gram plus char_wb 2-5gram TF-IDF, at 8.67% validation error against 10.0% for the word-only LR on the same split. The model blob (`133af59…`) and test code blob (`faff5f…`) are both in hand, so I'll publish the prediction claim with evidence from the sweep and final-training execs. My validation number is 8.67% on a 4k train split, and the README comparator (about 8%) is measured on the official test set, so the test is the real check. The claim will also state the within-split margin over word-only LR.

founder: published AG News prediction claim (LinearSVC word1-3+char_wb2-5, C=0.3). Within-split val error 8.67% vs word-only LR 9.98% on the same 4k split; the README comparator (~8%) is on the official test set and was not measured by us, so the evaluator's test is the decisive check.
I'll read the inbox and the artifact list to see the CIFAR researcher's progress and whether there is anything I should build on or correct.
Reading the CIFAR artifact tells me its evidence exec, weight blob, and test setup. That's what I'd need to extend it, for example with a flip-TTA or ensemble check, rather than duplicating its run.

Their 5.36% comes from a 5k holdout drawn from train. I'll inspect the released code to confirm the split and that no test or validation images leak into training. If it's clean, a seed-replication or ensemble check is a worthwhile next step.
The split logic is in the training script, not the prediction code. I'll find exec-53f6b41c's code blob and inspect how it partitions the 50k images.
A replication with a different seed tests whether 5.36% is stable or a lucky draw. I need to see how the script sets its seed and reads the data before I can change it.
Two extra seeds on the same 45k/5k split will show whether 5.36% is stable or a lucky draw. The runs are sequential to stay within the 900s block limit.
Waiting for the f60 exec to finish, then pulling the weights blob and exec id. I'll check its output before publishing anything.
Verify the metric and blob ids in `lab runs` for exec-85f0c995 and exec-ef86be67 before building the contribution, so every number in the claim matches a recorded exec.

Publish a second finding that builds on the 30-epoch one, using the 60-epoch holdout and full-data weights. It reuses the same predict.py test code, passes the weights as a dict input, and cites both execs.
The live checks passed for the 60-epoch finding, and the 30-epoch one is already accepted. I'll tell the board what I published and where the numbers come from, then check the artifact list.

cifar-researcher: published 2 findings. (1) 30 ep: holdout val_error 0.0536 (exec-53f6b41c), full-data weights exec-a5951729. (2) 60 ep: holdout val_error 0.0526 (exec-85f0c995), full-data weights exec-ef86be67, prediction test on cifar10 test set. Both use predict.py test code 03ea2588. Reference is 6%; no further claims planned unless someone needs the weights.
I need the exact `val_error` for each seed from the recorded execs, not from memory, before I can say whether 5.36% is stable.

The prediction test has only been run once, on random noise, through the training exec. I'll run predict.py as a separate exec with the weights passed via `--input`, then compare its predictions.csv with the training exec's predictions.csv blob.
The released `predict.py` loads weights from `IN_DIR/weights`, so my full-data run must write the same file name and format. I'll check how `run.py` saves weights and what `predict.py` expects.

Fix predict.py to read `$IN_DIR/weights` directly and fall back to any file. Re-run it with real train images (labels known) so I can check the pipeline gives a sensible accuracy, not just that it runs.

I'll patch a copy of the released script so the no-EVAL branch trains on all 50k and saves fp16 weights into `OUT_DIR/weights/`. I'll then fetch that weights blob, repackage it as a directory with `weights.pt`, and store it for the released test code.

Put the fixed predict.py into a new test blob, get the id of the verify exec, and contribute a corrective finding. I'll cite the verify exec as evidence and point a `corrects` relation at the 60-epoch finding.
Read the baselines README to see what "beats the comparator" means for a prediction test, then list artifacts to confirm the corrective finding is live.

The baselines README confirms the cifar10 prediction claims must beat 6% error, so the corrective finding targets the right comparator. The original 30-epoch finding (`findin-66ecab68`) still points at the broken test blob `03ea2588`, and so does the 60-epoch finding (`findin-118c1f94`). I'll post a board note that the corrected blob `9d84193e` supersedes both and that the original test code will fail.

cifar-researcher: WARNING for anyone reading my CIFAR findings. Test code blob 03ea2588 (used by findin-66ecab68 and findin-118c1f94) looks for a *.pt file in IN_DIR, but the evaluator mounts test inputs as a file named 'weights', so its prediction test will fail. Corrected predict.py is blob 9d84193e (finding findin-c842cddf, verified by exec-877761f0). Use 9d84193e for the CIFAR prediction test. Reported numbers are holdout val error on 5k train images, not official-test error; the 6% comparator is only checked by the evaluator.

The corrected prediction test is live and the board has the warning. I'm at about 21 minutes of the 60 and have no official-test labels, so I can't measure the test error myself. A bigger run would add risk for a small gain. I'll record the final state and end my part of the session.

The released predictor loads `$IN_DIR/weights.pt` when no `weights/` directory exists, so the input must be named `weights.pt`. The `replicates` relation requires the used blob to be consumed in `test.inputs`.

founder: replication of findin-66ecab68 (CIFAR ResNet-9). Same holdout split, seed 1 -> 5.50%, seed 2 -> 5.70% (exec-5494c8ef, exec-c85b3568). Seed-1 model trained on all 50k (exec-2b8bde34) scored by the released predict.py on the official test set. Relation: replicates.
Nothing has been posted since my last check. I'll read the inbox and artifact list, then wait for messages or new contributions rather than spend more compute blindly.

This checks my own claim's test path before the evaluator runs it. The mock set uses 1,000 training images, so the accuracy is not meaningful. The check is only that the predictor loads the weights and writes predictions.

founder: checked my replication's test path. The released predict.py (blob 03ea2588) loads IN_DIR/weights.pt when no weights/ dir exists; findin-89e9d821 mounts its input as 'weights.pt', so it does not hit the 'weights' mismatch the CIFAR researcher reported. Verification run on a mock 1k eval set is in the lab exec log (verify.py, input weights.pt=f97de132). Thanks for the warning; findin-66ecab68 and findin-118c1f94 need blob 9d84193e.

A 5-fold CV on all 40k articles gives a more reliable margin than the single 4k split. I'll compare my LinearSVC configuration with a plain word-1-2gram TF-IDF+LR, which approximates the README comparator.
Run the same 5-fold split with stronger LR variants (different C, and word+char features) to see the best LR the evaluator's comparator could plausibly be.
A comparison test is the right tool: arm A is my saved SVM, arm B is the strong LR retrained on all 40k inside the test. I'll verify the script on a mock eval set, then gather the CV exec ids.

The comparison claim needs arm A (saved SVM) to beat arm B (strong LR retrained inside the test). Quantities come from the recorded CV execs, and the test uses the same `cmp.py` I verified on a mock set.

founder: published AG News comparison claim (findin via /work/f_cmp.json). Arm A: LinearSVC word1-3+char (C=0.3); arm B: LR word1-2+char (C=10), retrained on 40k inside the test. 5-fold CV: 8.13% vs 8.70%. Strongest LR we tried, so this is the honest margin. Test code blob 5fe7f12e.
Several claims now depend on my CV numbers and on the released CIFAR test code. I need to see whether anyone has raised issues before I decide whether to wait or finish.
Further runs would add little. The remaining value is in responding to others' work, so I'll pause until a message or contribution arrives.

I'll post a status note that separates what is verified from what is still open, then finish. The first AG News claim is the weakest: its margin was measured on a 4k split against a word-only LR, not against the README comparator on the official test set.

founder: status. Contributions: (1) findin-91ae53ea AG News LinearSVC, 8.67% on a 4k split vs 9.98% word-only LR on the same split.
